overview.headline: How DNA stores hereditary information and copies itself

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA is the hereditary material found in humans and most other organisms.
keyPoints.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that human DNA contains about 3 billion bases and most bases are the same in all people.
keyPoints.quote: Human DNA consists of about 3 billion bases, and more than 99 percent of those bases are the same in all people.

keyPoints.point: Students learn how DNA bases pair into units called base pairs with specific partners.
keyPoints.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA can replicate to make copies of itself when cells divide.
keyPoints.quote: An important property of DNA is that it can replicate, or make copies of itself.

keyTerms.gloss: a chemical base that stores information in DNA
keyTerms.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).

keyTerms.gloss: paired units formed when bases pair with partners
keyTerms.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyTerms.gloss: unit made from a base, sugar and phosphate
keyTerms.quote: Together, a base, sugar, and phosphate are called a nucleotide.

keyTerms.gloss: spiral shape formed by two long strands
keyTerms.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.

keyTerms.gloss: structures within cells that convert energy from food
keyTerms.quote: Mitochondria are structures within cells that convert the energy from food into a form that cells can use.
